results.question: What are the main ingredients of a Colombian ajiaco?
results.reply_text:
Main ingredients of a Colombian Ajiaco (Bogotano)



Category
Ingredients (typical)




Protein
• 1 whole chicken (or 4 bone‑in chicken breasts/thighs)


Potatoes
• 3 kinds of potatoes:  – 1 lb (≈ 450 g) papa criolla (yellow/Andean potatoes)  – 1 lb (≈ 450 g) papa sabanera (red potatoes)  – 1 lb (≈ 450 g) papa pastosa (white or russet potatoes)


Vegetables & Corn
• 3 ears of fresh corn, cut into 3‑inch pieces • 1 medium onion, chopped • 3–4 garlic cloves, minced


Herb
• Guascas (dried herb, essential for the distinctive flavor)


Spices & Seasoning
• Salt • Bay leaves (2–3) • Cumin (optional, for extra depth)


Liquid Base
• Chicken broth or water (≈ 10 cups / 2.4 L)


Garnishes (served with)
• Capers (drained) • Sliced avocado • Sour cream or crema • Fresh cilantro or parsley • White rice (often served on the side)



Brief preparation note:

Simmer the chicken in broth with potatoes, corn, onion, garlic, guascas, bay leaves, and salt until the meat is tender.
Add the potatoes gradually so they thicken the soup naturally.
Remove the chicken, shred the meat, and return it to the pot.
Serve hot with the garnishes (capers, avocado, sour cream) and a side of rice.

These ingredients are consistently highlighted across multiple authentic Colombian recipe sources (e.g., My Colombian Recipes, Que Are Pas, My Planet Food, Immigrant Stable, Colombian Recipes).
nyas: That hearty mix makes ajiaco the perfect comfort food for cool Andean days!
